limitations_and_boundaries: The study uses mouse models and in vitro systems; human relevance may require further validation.
The feed-forward loop model is proposed based on correlative and perturbation data; direct causal evidence for each step is not fully established.
The selected source chunks do not report a rescue, reconstitution, reversal, or epistasis experiment; that rung of the causal evidence chain remains untested within this extraction scope.

missed_core_items.description: The extraction omits the central finding that YAP regulates MYL9 protein levels post-transcriptionally, which is critical for CAF function.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: We also found that MYL9 and MYH10 are required for CAF functionality (Fig. 5b,c and see Supplementary Fig. S4e for multiple siRNA). These genes are not transcriptionally regulated by YAP; nonetheless we explored whether their protein levels depend on YAP. Figure 5d shows that depletion of YAP, but not TAZ, reduces both the total levels of MYL9 and MYH10 and the level of active Ser 19 phosphorylated MYL9.

missed_core_items.description: The extraction omits the key result that acute inhibition of ROCK, myosin, and Src reduces YAP nuclear localization even after matrix remodelling, demonstrating that actomyosin and Src are required for YAP maintenance.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: To explicitly test the latter hypothesis, we allowed CAFs three days to remodel the collagen-rich matrix and then acutely treated with inhibitors (Fig. 7a). These experiments reveal that ROCK, myosin and Src function (blocked by PP2 and dasatinib) are required to maintain the nuclear localization of YAP in CAFs, even after the ECM has been remodelled.

missed_core_items.description: The extraction omits the result that YAP depletion reduces focal adhesions, which is a key functional consequence.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: YAP-depleted cells also had fewer focal adhesions, essential structures for force transmission between the cytoskeleton and matrix (Fig. 4b).

missed_core_items.description: The extraction omits the result that YAP depletion reduces thick collagen fibres and elastic modulus, which is a central quantitative finding.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: These defects were associated with fewer thick collagen fibres within matrices containing YAP-depleted cells together with a lower elastic modulus (Fig. 4c).

missed_core_items.description: The extraction omits the result that YAP activation in NFs (via YAP S5A or MST1/2 depletion) increases invasion-promoting ability, which is a key gain-of-function experiment.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: Conversely, activation of YAP signalling by either overexpression of an active mutant or depletion of MST1&2 increased invasion-promoting ability of NFs (Supplementary Fig. S4b,g).

missed_core_items.description: The extraction omits the result that conditioned media from cancer cells promotes YAP nuclear translocation and target gene activation in NFs, which is a key step in the proposed model.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: This change in behaviour was also associated with the nuclear translocation of YAP and the activation of some YAP/TAZ target genes (Fig. 6b,c).

missed_core_items.description: The extraction omits the result that increasing collagen matrix stiffness drives YAP nuclear accumulation in NFs, which is a key control experiment.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: Finally, we confirmed previous findings12 that increasing collagen matrix stiffness is sufficient to drive the nuclear accumulation of YAP in NFs (Fig. 6g).

missed_core_items.description: The extraction omits the result that ROCK inhibition reduces Src activity, which is a key mechanistic link.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: Further, ROCK inhibition reduced Src activity (Supplementary Fig. S5e).

missed_core_items.description: The extraction omits the result that YAP is regulated at the level of interaction with TEAD and 14-3-3 proteins, not through canonical MST/LATS phosphorylation, which is a central mechanistic finding.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: Together, these data argue that YAP is not activated by reduced activity of the canonical MST1/2–LATS pathways in CAFs. Instead, YAP is regulated at the level of interaction with TEAD and 14-3-3 proteins.

missed_core_items.description: The extraction omits the result that YAP nuclear localization is a universal feature of CAFs regardless of αSMA, FAP, or S100A4 expression, which is a key characterization finding.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: Nuclear localization of YAP was a universal feature of CAFs, regardless of their expression levels of αSMA, FAP or S100A4 (Supplementary Fig. S3d, also compare Supplementary Figs S2c and S3c).
